title: 10,000 workers to go to Malaysia at low cost, PM tells parliament
excerpt: Tarique Rahman said 1,000 places are set aside for families of victims of enforced disappearance and the July uprising, and syndicates will face action.
content:
Ten thousand Bangladeshi workers will go to Malaysia at almost no cost, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman told parliament on Wednesday (18 November), The Financial Express reported. About 1,000 of the places are set aside for families of victims of enforced disappearance and killings under the previous government, and of people killed or injured in the 2024 uprising.

bdnews24.com reported that the total cost would be capped at Tk 200,000 per worker. The prime minister said the government was identifying the "syndicates that cheated people" and that recruitment syndicates had nearly led some countries to stop hiring Bangladeshis.

Zero-cost hiring

He was answering a question from Kamrul Hasan, MP for Mymensingh-6. He said talks were also under way with Middle Eastern countries. Separately, Malaysian glove maker Top Glove said in a press release that it was promoting "100 per cent zero-cost recruitment" for Bangladeshi workers, The Financial Express reported.

Why it matters

High recruitment fees push migrant workers into debt and raise the risk of forced labour and trafficking. Migrant rights NGOs will want to see how the cost cap is enforced and whether workers get written contracts before they leave.

What to watch

How the 10,000 workers are selected, whether the cap covers all fees, and any action against recruiting agencies.
